questions.question: What is Angular?
questions.answer: Angular is a TypeScript-based framework for building web applications. Developed by Google. Provides complete solution with routing, forms, HTTP, and testing.

questions.question: What is the difference between Angular and AngularJS?
questions.answer: Angular is complete rewrite of AngularJS. Uses TypeScript, component-based, better performance, improved tooling. AngularJS is older, uses JavaScript.

questions.question: What are Angular components?
questions.answer: Components are building blocks of Angular apps. Contain template, styles, and logic. Decorated with @Component. Enable modularity and reusability.

questions.question: What is data binding in Angular?
questions.answer: Data binding connects component data to template. One-way: {{ }}, property binding, event binding. Two-way: [(ngModel)]. Automatically updates on changes.

questions.question: What are directives in Angular?
questions.answer: Directives modify DOM behavior. Structural: *ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch. Attribute: ngClass, ngStyle. Custom directives extend functionality.

questions.question: What is *ngIf?
questions.answer: *ngIf conditionally renders element. Removes from DOM if false. Syntax: *ngIf='condition'. Better for infrequent toggles.

questions.question: What is *ngFor?
questions.answer: *ngFor renders list of items. Syntax: *ngFor='let item of items'. Can use index: *ngFor='let item of items; let i = index'. Always use trackBy for performance.

questions.question: What is *ngSwitch?
questions.answer: *ngSwitch conditionally renders based on value. Syntax: *ngSwitchCase='value'. More readable than multiple *ngIf. Includes *ngSwitchDefault.

questions.question: What is [ngClass]?
questions.answer: [ngClass] dynamically adds CSS classes. Syntax: [ngClass]='{ active: isActive }'. Can use object or string. Enables conditional styling.

questions.question: What is [ngStyle]?
questions.answer: [ngStyle] dynamically adds inline styles. Syntax: [ngStyle]='{ color: activeColor }'. Enables dynamic styling based on data.

questions.question: What are template-driven forms?
questions.answer: Template-driven forms use directives in template. Two-way binding with ngModel. Simpler for basic forms. Less control than reactive forms.

questions.question: What are reactive forms?
questions.answer: Reactive forms use FormBuilder in component. More control and flexibility. Better for complex forms. Enables dynamic form creation.

questions.question: What are Angular services?
questions.answer: Services provide shared logic across components. Decorated with @Injectable(). Enable dependency injection. Useful for API calls and data sharing.

questions.question: What is dependency injection in Angular?
questions.answer: Dependency injection provides dependencies to components. Reduces coupling and improves testability. Declared in constructor. Managed by Angular injector.

questions.question: What is Angular Router?
questions.answer: Router enables navigation between components. Maps URLs to components. Provides lazy loading and guards. Uses RouterModule and Routes.

questions.question: What are route guards?
questions.answer: Guards protect routes from unauthorized access. CanActivate, CanDeactivate, CanLoad. Implement interfaces and return boolean or Observable.

questions.question: What is HttpClient in Angular?
questions.answer: HttpClient makes HTTP requests. Provides methods: get, post, put, delete. Returns Observable. Requires HttpClientModule.

questions.question: What are Observables in Angular?
questions.answer: Observables represent async data streams. Used with HttpClient and events. Provide operators like map, filter, subscribe. Better than Promises for multiple values.

questions.question: What are RxJS operators?
questions.answer: Operators transform Observable streams. Examples: map, filter, switchMap, mergeMap. Enable functional programming style. Chainable for complex operations.

questions.question: What are pipes in Angular?
questions.answer: Pipes format data in templates. Built-in: date, currency, uppercase, lowercase. Custom pipes implement PipeTransform. Syntax: {{ value | pipeName }}.

questions.question: What are Angular modules?
questions.answer: Modules organize related components, services, directives. Decorated with @NgModule. Declare components, import dependencies. Enable code organization.

questions.question: What is lazy loading in Angular?
questions.answer: Lazy loading loads modules on demand. Improves initial load time. Configured in routing. Syntax: { path: 'feature', loadChildren: () => import('./feature/feature.module').then(m => m.FeatureModule) }.

questions.question: What are Angular lifecycle hooks?
questions.answer: Lifecycle hooks execute at specific stages. ngOnInit, ngOnChanges, ngOnDestroy, etc. Implement OnInit, OnDestroy interfaces. Enable initialization and cleanup.

questions.question: What is ngOnInit?
questions.answer: ngOnInit runs after component initialization. Best place for initialization logic. Called once after first ngOnChanges. Implement OnInit interface.

questions.question: What is ngOnDestroy?
questions.answer: ngOnDestroy runs before component destruction. Best place for cleanup (unsubscribe, clear timers). Called when component is removed. Implement OnDestroy interface.

questions.question: What is @Input?
questions.answer: @Input passes data from parent to child. Read-only in child. Syntax: @Input() message: string. Enables parent-child communication.

questions.question: What is @Output?
questions.answer: @Output emits events from child to parent. Uses EventEmitter. Syntax: @Output() messageEvent = new EventEmitter(). Enables child-parent communication.

questions.question: What are custom directives?
questions.answer: Custom directives extend HTML functionality. Structural or attribute directives. Decorated with @Directive. Implement logic for DOM manipulation.

questions.question: What is @Component?
questions.answer: @Component decorator defines component. Specifies selector, template, styles. Syntax: @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: '...' }). Required for components.

questions.question: What is @Injectable?
questions.answer: @Injectable decorator marks class as service. Enables dependency injection. Syntax: @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }). Required for services.

questions.question: What is @Directive?
questions.answer: @Directive decorator defines directive. Specifies selector. Syntax: @Directive({ selector: '[appHighlight]' }). Required for directives.

questions.question: What is @NgModule?
questions.answer: @NgModule decorator defines module. Specifies declarations, imports, providers, exports. Syntax: @NgModule({ declarations: [...] }). Required for modules.

questions.question: What is @HostListener?
questions.answer: @HostListener listens to host element events. Syntax: @HostListener('click') onClick() {}. Enables event handling in directives.

questions.question: What is @HostBinding?
questions.answer: @HostBinding binds to host element properties. Syntax: @HostBinding('class.active') isActive = true. Enables property binding in directives.

questions.question: What is @ViewChild?
questions.answer: @ViewChild gets reference to child component. Syntax: @ViewChild(ChildComponent) child: ChildComponent. Enables parent-child interaction.

questions.question: What is @ViewChildren?
questions.answer: @ViewChildren gets references to multiple child components. Syntax: @ViewChildren(ChildComponent) children: QueryList<ChildComponent>. Returns QueryList.

questions.question: What is @ContentChild?
questions.answer: @ContentChild gets reference to projected content. Syntax: @ContentChild(ChildComponent) child: ChildComponent. Enables content projection.

questions.question: What is @ContentChildren?
questions.answer: @ContentChildren gets references to multiple projected content. Syntax: @ContentChildren(ChildComponent) children: QueryList<ChildComponent>. Returns QueryList.

questions.question: What is change detection in Angular?
questions.answer: Change detection updates DOM when data changes. Default: CheckAlways. OnPush: manual control. Affects performance. Can be optimized with ChangeDetectionStrategy.

questions.question: What is ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush?
questions.answer: OnPush strategy manually triggers change detection. Only checks when @Input changes or events fire. Improves performance for large apps.

questions.question: What is property binding?
questions.answer: Property binding sets element properties. Syntax: [property]='value'. One-way binding from component to template. Updates when value changes.

questions.question: What is event binding?
questions.answer: Event binding listens to element events. Syntax: (event)='method()'. One-way binding from template to component. Triggers method on event.

questions.question: What is two-way binding?
questions.answer: Two-way binding combines property and event binding. Syntax: [(ngModel)]='property'. Updates both directions. Requires FormsModule.

questions.question: What is attribute binding?
questions.answer: Attribute binding sets HTML attributes. Syntax: [attr.aria-label]='label'. Used for attributes without properties. Useful for accessibility.

questions.question: What is class binding?
questions.answer: Class binding adds/removes CSS classes. Syntax: [class.active]='isActive'. Can use [ngClass] for multiple classes. Enables conditional styling.

questions.question: What is style binding?
questions.answer: Style binding sets inline styles. Syntax: [style.color]='color'. Can use [ngStyle] for multiple styles. Enables dynamic styling.

questions.question: What is string interpolation?
questions.answer: String interpolation displays component data. Syntax: {{ expression }}. One-way binding. Evaluates expressions in template context.

questions.question: What is FormBuilder?
questions.answer: FormBuilder creates form groups and controls. Syntax: this.fb.group({ name: ['', Validators.required] }). Simplifies reactive form creation.

questions.question: What are form validators?
questions.answer: Validators check form control values. Built-in: required, minLength, maxLength, pattern. Custom validators implement ValidatorFn. Used in reactive forms.

questions.question: What is form validation?
questions.answer: Form validation checks input validity. Validators run on form controls. Provides error messages. Enables form submission control.

questions.question: What is subscribe in Angular?
questions.answer: subscribe() listens to Observable emissions. Syntax: observable.subscribe(value => {}). Returns Subscription. Must unsubscribe to prevent memory leaks.

questions.question: What is unsubscribe in Angular?
questions.answer: unsubscribe() stops listening to Observable. Prevents memory leaks. Called in ngOnDestroy. Can use takeUntil operator for automatic cleanup.

questions.question: What is the async pipe?
questions.answer: async pipe subscribes to Observable in template. Syntax: {{ observable | async }}. Automatically unsubscribes on destroy. Simplifies Observable handling.

questions.question: What are HTTP interceptors?
questions.answer: Interceptors modify HTTP requests/responses. Implement HttpInterceptor. Useful for authentication, logging, error handling. Registered in providers.

questions.question: What is a singleton service?
questions.answer: Singleton service has one instance across app. Declared with providedIn: 'root'. Shared across components. Useful for global state.

questions.question: What is a scoped service?
questions.answer: Scoped service has instance per component. Declared in component providers. Not shared with other components. Useful for component-specific state.

questions.question: What is TestBed in Angular?
questions.answer: TestBed configures testing module. Syntax: TestBed.configureTestingModule({ declarations: [...] }). Enables component testing with dependencies.

questions.question: What is fixture in Angular testing?
questions.answer: fixture provides access to component instance and DOM. Syntax: const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(Component). Enables component testing.

questions.question: What is ComponentFixture?
questions.answer: ComponentFixture wraps component for testing. Provides debugElement, componentInstance, nativeElement. Enables DOM and component testing.

questions.question: What is ActivatedRoute?
questions.answer: ActivatedRoute provides access to route parameters. Syntax: constructor(private route: ActivatedRoute) {}. Enables access to URL parameters and query strings.

questions.question: What is Router?
questions.answer: Router enables navigation between routes. Syntax: constructor(private router: Router) {}. Methods: navigate(), navigateByUrl(). Enables programmatic navigation.

questions.question: What is SharedModule?
questions.answer: SharedModule contains shared components, directives, pipes. Imported by feature modules. Reduces duplication. Enables code reuse.

questions.question: What is CoreModule?
questions.answer: CoreModule contains singleton services and core components. Imported once in AppModule. Prevents duplicate service instances.

questions.question: What is FeatureModule?
questions.answer: FeatureModule contains feature-specific components and services. Lazy loaded or eagerly loaded. Enables code organization and lazy loading.

questions.question: What is [ngIf]?
questions.answer: [ngIf] is property binding for *ngIf. Syntax: [ngIf]='condition'. Removes element from DOM if false. Less common than *ngIf.

questions.question: What is [ngFor]?
questions.answer: [ngFor] is property binding for *ngFor. Syntax: [ngForOf]='items'. Renders list of items. Less common than *ngFor.

questions.question: What is [ngSwitch]?
questions.answer: [ngSwitch] is property binding for *ngSwitch. Syntax: [ngSwitch]='value'. Conditionally renders based on value. Less common than *ngSwitch.

questions.question: What is the date pipe?
questions.answer: date pipe formats dates. Syntax: {{ date | date:'short' }}. Supports various formats. Useful for date display.

questions.question: What is the currency pipe?
questions.answer: currency pipe formats currency values. Syntax: {{ amount | currency:'USD' }}. Supports various currencies. Useful for money display.

questions.question: What is the uppercase pipe?
questions.answer: uppercase pipe converts text to uppercase. Syntax: {{ text | uppercase }}. Simple text transformation. Built-in pipe.

questions.question: What is the lowercase pipe?
questions.answer: lowercase pipe converts text to lowercase. Syntax: {{ text | lowercase }}. Simple text transformation. Built-in pipe.

questions.question: What is the slice pipe?
questions.answer: slice pipe extracts substring or subarray. Syntax: {{ text | slice:0:5 }}. Supports start and end indices. Useful for truncation.

questions.question: What is the json pipe?
questions.answer: json pipe converts object to JSON string. Syntax: {{ object | json }}. Useful for debugging. Shows object structure.

questions.question: What is the decimal pipe?
questions.answer: decimal pipe formats numbers. Syntax: {{ number | number:'1.2-2' }}. Supports digit info. Useful for number formatting.

questions.question: What is the percent pipe?
questions.answer: percent pipe formats percentages. Syntax: {{ value | percent }}. Multiplies by 100 and adds %. Useful for percentage display.

questions.question: What is a custom pipe?
questions.answer: Custom pipe implements PipeTransform. Decorated with @Pipe. Syntax: @Pipe({ name: 'custom' }). Enables custom data formatting.

questions.question: What is a structural directive?
questions.answer: Structural directive changes DOM structure. Syntax: *ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch. Prefixed with *. Adds or removes elements from DOM.

questions.question: What is an attribute directive?
questions.answer: Attribute directive changes element appearance or behavior. Syntax: [ngClass], [ngStyle]. No * prefix. Modifies existing elements.

questions.question: What is content projection?
questions.answer: Content projection passes content to child component. Uses <ng-content>. Enables flexible component composition. Syntax: <ng-content></ng-content>.

questions.question: What is ng-container?
questions.answer: <ng-container> is logical container without rendering. Useful for *ngIf without extra div. Enables conditional rendering without DOM impact.

questions.question: What is ng-template?
questions.answer: <ng-template> defines template not rendered by default. Used with *ngIf, *ngFor. Enables conditional template rendering.

questions.question: What is ngOnChanges?
questions.answer: ngOnChanges runs when @Input properties change. Receives SimpleChanges object. Called before ngOnInit. Implement OnChanges interface.

questions.question: What is ngDoCheck?
questions.answer: ngDoCheck runs on every change detection cycle. Detects changes Angular cannot. Called after ngOnChanges and ngOnInit. Implement DoCheck interface.

questions.question: What is ngAfterContentInit?
questions.answer: ngAfterContentInit runs after content projection. Called after ngDoCheck. Useful for accessing projected content. Implement AfterContentInit interface.

questions.question: What is ngAfterContentChecked?
questions.answer: ngAfterContentChecked runs after content check. Called after ngAfterContentInit. Useful for responding to content changes. Implement AfterContentChecked interface.

questions.question: What is ngAfterViewInit?
questions.answer: ngAfterViewInit runs after view initialization. Called after ngAfterContentChecked. Useful for accessing child components. Implement AfterViewInit interface.

questions.question: What is ngAfterViewChecked?
questions.answer: ngAfterViewChecked runs after view check. Called after ngAfterViewInit. Useful for responding to view changes. Implement AfterViewChecked interface.

questions.question: What is map operator?
questions.answer: map operator transforms Observable values. Syntax: observable.pipe(map(x => x * 2)). Returns new Observable with transformed values.

questions.question: What is filter operator?
questions.answer: filter operator filters Observable values. Syntax: observable.pipe(filter(x => x > 5)). Returns Observable with filtered values.

questions.question: What is switchMap operator?
questions.answer: switchMap operator switches to new Observable. Syntax: observable.pipe(switchMap(x => getDetails(x))). Cancels previous Observable. Useful for dependent requests.

questions.question: What is mergeMap operator?
questions.answer: mergeMap operator merges Observables. Syntax: observable.pipe(mergeMap(x => getDetails(x))). Doesn't cancel previous Observable. Useful for parallel requests.

questions.question: What is concatMap operator?
questions.answer: concatMap operator concatenates Observables in order. Syntax: observable.pipe(concatMap(x => getDetails(x))). Maintains order. Useful for sequential requests.

questions.question: What is takeUntil operator?
questions.answer: takeUntil operator stops Observable on signal. Syntax: observable.pipe(takeUntil(destroy$)). Useful for automatic unsubscription. Prevents memory leaks.

questions.question: What is debounceTime operator?
questions.answer: debounceTime operator delays emissions. Syntax: observable.pipe(debounceTime(300)). Useful for search input. Reduces API calls.

questions.question: What is distinctUntilChanged operator?
questions.answer: distinctUntilChanged operator filters duplicate consecutive values. Syntax: observable.pipe(distinctUntilChanged()). Useful for preventing redundant operations.

questions.question: What is combineLatest operator?
questions.answer: combineLatest operator combines multiple Observables. Syntax: combineLatest([obs1, obs2]). Emits latest values from all. Useful for dependent data.

questions.question: What is merge operator?
questions.answer: merge operator merges multiple Observables. Syntax: merge(obs1, obs2). Emits from any source. Useful for handling multiple events.

questions.question: What is forkJoin operator?
questions.answer: forkJoin operator waits for all Observables. Syntax: forkJoin([obs1, obs2]). Emits when all complete. Useful for parallel requests.

questions.question: What is tap operator?
questions.answer: tap operator performs side effects. Syntax: observable.pipe(tap(x => console.log(x))). Doesn't modify values. Useful for debugging.

questions.question: What is catchError operator?
questions.answer: catchError operator handles Observable errors. Syntax: observable.pipe(catchError(err => of(null))). Returns fallback Observable. Enables error recovery.
